items.followUp: What is the purpose of the <body> tag in an HTML document?

rubric.why: Identifies what the title specifies and where it is displayed.
rubric.description: States that the <title> tag sets the webpage’s title, shown in the browser tab or title bar.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly naming the title and its browser display location.

rubric.why: Shows understanding of the tag’s place in an HTML document.
rubric.description: States that the <title> tag is placed inside the <head> section.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the <head> section.

modelAnswer: The <title> tag specifies the title or name of an HTML document.
The title is displayed in the browser tab or title bar and is written inside the <head> section.

items.followUp: Define a flowchart and state one benefit of using it.

rubric.why: A definition should convey that an algorithm is a bounded, ordered procedure for solving a problem.
rubric.description: Defines an algorithm as a finite sequence of clear, ordered steps for solving a problem or performing a task.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a complete definition; award 1 mark if it identifies steps for solving a problem but omits finiteness or clarity.

rubric.why: Efficiency is assessed through the resources an algorithm uses.
rubric.description: Explains that efficiency is determined by the time and memory (space) required, often by considering how these change as input size increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for time/number of operations and 1 mark for memory/space, or 2 marks for explaining both in relation to input size.

modelAnswer: An algorithm is a finite sequence of clear, ordered steps used to solve a problem or perform a task.
The efficiency of an algorithm is determined by the time it takes and the memory (space) it uses.
These resources can be compared for different input sizes, using the number of operations and memory required.

items.followUp: Describe bus and ring network topologies.

rubric.why: The central connecting device is the defining feature of a star topology.
rubric.description: States that every device in a star topology connects to a central hub or switch.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the central connection correctly.

rubric.why: Shows how communication or a failure is handled in a star network.
rubric.description: Explains that data passes through the central device, or that failure of the hub/switch disrupts the network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct operational feature or consequence of central-device failure.

rubric.why: A mesh is characterized by direct connections among its nodes.
rubric.description: States that in a mesh topology each node is connected directly to every other node (or to many other nodes in a partial mesh).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the interconnections.

rubric.why: A key feature of mesh topology is its redundancy, balanced against the cost of many links.
rubric.description: Gives a valid feature or drawback of mesh, such as reliability through alternative paths or high cabling cost.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one accurate advantage or disadvantage.

modelAnswer: In a star topology, every computer or device is connected to a central hub or switch.
Data sent between devices passes through this central device; if it fails, the network is disrupted.
In a mesh topology, each node is connected directly to every other node in a full mesh, providing multiple paths for data.
Mesh networks are reliable if a link fails, but require many connections and can be expensive.

items.followUp: Explain the Caesar cipher and encrypt the word CAT using a shift of 2.

rubric.why: This is the defining operation of a substitution cipher.
rubric.description: Explains that a substitution cipher encrypts plaintext by replacing its letters or symbols with other letters or symbols.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for clearly describing replacement/substitution.

rubric.why: A fixed mapping describes the monoalphabetic substitution method.
rubric.description: Describes monoalphabetic substitution as using the same fixed letter mapping throughout the message.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the fixed-mapping method.

rubric.why: A changing mapping based on a key is the other common substitution method.
rubric.description: Describes polyalphabetic substitution as using multiple substitution alphabets or changing substitutions according to a key.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the method.

rubric.why: A correct worked example demonstrates how substitution is applied.
rubric.description: Gives a correct Caesar-cipher example using a shift of three, such as HELLO becoming KHOOR.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct plaintext, shift, and ciphertext example.

modelAnswer: A substitution cipher encrypts a message by replacing each plaintext letter with another letter according to a rule or key.
In monoalphabetic substitution, the same fixed substitution is used throughout the message.
In polyalphabetic substitution, the substitutions can change according to a key or multiple substitution alphabets.
For example, a Caesar cipher shifts each letter three places: HELLO becomes KHOOR.

items.followUp: Write two advantages of using a flowchart to plan a program.

rubric.why: A flowchart makes a process easier to see and understand.
rubric.description: Gives the advantage that a flowchart presents the steps visually and makes the process easy to understand.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one clear understanding or visualization benefit.

rubric.why: Flowcharts also support communication, checking, or recording a solution.
rubric.description: Gives another valid advantage, such as communicating logic, finding errors, or documenting a solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct, valid advantage.

modelAnswer: A flowchart shows the steps of a solution visually, making the process easier to understand.
It helps communicate the solution and can make errors easier to find.

items.followUp: What is valid test data? Give one example.

rubric.why: Invalid test data must fail at least one stated input condition.
rubric.description: Defines invalid test data as data that does not satisfy the program’s input requirements, such as being outside the permitted range or having the wrong type.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that the data violates an input requirement.

rubric.why: Invalid data is used to check that a program handles unacceptable input correctly.
rubric.description: States that invalid test data checks whether the program detects or rejects unacceptable input.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining its testing purpose.

modelAnswer: Invalid test data is input that does not meet the program’s requirements, such as a value outside an allowed range.
It is used to check that the program detects or rejects unacceptable input.

items.followUp: What does a terminal symbol show in a flowchart?

rubric.why: A connector links flowchart sections or indicates that the flow continues elsewhere.
rubric.description: States that a connector links separated parts of a flowchart or indicates continuation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly explaining the connector’s linking or continuation role.

rubric.why: Connectors make flowcharts easier to follow, especially when lines would otherwise be long or cross.
rubric.description: Gives a correct use, such as avoiding crossing/long flow lines or connecting to a point on the same or another page.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid explanation of when or why a connector is used.

modelAnswer: A connector is used to link separated parts of a flowchart or to show where the flow continues.
It helps avoid long or crossing flow lines and can connect sections on the same or another page.

items.followUp: How can a diagram help you identify the information needed to solve a problem?

rubric.why: Drawing a picture represents the problem in a visible form that can be examined.
rubric.description: Explains that drawing a picture gives a visual representation of the problem or situation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the visual representation.

rubric.why: A visual representation can reveal relevant details and how they relate to one another.
rubric.description: Explains that the picture helps identify important details, relationships, or known and unknown information, making the problem easier to understand.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid explanation of how the picture aids problem definition.

modelAnswer: Drawing a picture gives a visual representation of the problem or situation.
It can make important details and relationships clearer and help identify what is known and what needs to be found.
